reason: The base image is passed in as a tag by design: the verified mirror on main, the upstream tag on pull requests, rebuilt daily so it picks up the base's security updates (docs/adr/0001, 0007, 0008). The mirror step verifies the digest it copies.

npm is pinned to an exact version by ARG NPM_VERSION, which scripts/check-pins.sh tracks and the pin-bump bot moves (docs/adr/0007); Scorecard only accepts a hash, which npm install --global cannot take.

Single-maintainer repository: automated PRs are merged by the merge bot only after the four required checks pass on their head commit (docs/adr/0008), so most changesets have no human approval by design.
Nothing to fuzz: the repository is Dockerfiles, shell scripts and workflows, with no parser or library code of its own.
The OpenSSF Best Practices badge is an optional self-certification this repository has not applied for.

main is protected by the `main` ruleset (no deletion, no force push, pull requests required, the four required checks, admin bypass only). Scorecard's top tiers also need two or more approving reviewers and code-owner review, which a single-maintainer repository cannot have, so the check never reaches 10 here. The scorecard-upload job drops this entry, and the alert shows again, whenever main stops having any of those rules.
